Differential Abundance Testing

Source: R/da_test.r
da_test.Rd

Runs any of ecodive's differential-abundance (DA) methods by name, as count_ord() does for ordinations, with one convention for the groups or model to compare.

Usage

da_test(counts, method, groups = NULL, data = NULL, formula = NULL, ...)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of non-negative abundances (samples \(\times\) features), or any of the objects listed under Input Types.

method

The name of a DA method: "ancom", "ancombc", "ancombc2", "da_lm", "da_ttest", "da_wilcoxon", "dirmult_ttest", or "linda". Flexible matching is supported (see below). Programmatic access via list_da_tests().

groups

The grouping to compare: the name of a column of data, or a vector with one value per sample. For a model method, the term of interest: alone, it is the model (formula = ~ groups); with formula, it names one of its terms (see below).

data

A data frame of sample metadata, with a row per sample, matched to the samples of counts by name when both have names, else by position.

formula

For a model method (design = "formula" in list_da_tests()), the model: a one-sided formula over the columns of data, such as ~ status + age. A group method takes a formula of one variable, ~ status, as groups = "status".

...

Further arguments for the method's function, such as margin, alpha, p_adjust, cpus, contrast (da_ttest(), da_wilcoxon(), dirmult_ttest()), norm and pseudocount. Each method keeps its own defaults; see ancom(), ancombc(), ancombc2(), da_lm(), da_ttest(), da_wilcoxon(), dirmult_ttest(), and linda(). seed is ignored by the methods that have no random parts (all but dirmult_ttest()).

Value

The method's result, unchanged: da_test(counts, 'ancombc2', ...) is identical to ancombc2(counts, ...), attributes included. Every result is a data frame with a row per feature (and covariate, for the model methods) and a method attribute, the method's id.

Details

List of DA Methods

Option / Function NameMethod NameDesign
ancomAnalysis of Composition of Microbiomes (ANCOM)groups
ancombcANCOM with bias correction (ANCOM-BC)formula
ancombc2ANCOM-BC2formula
da_lmLinear model per featureformula
da_ttestWelch t-test per featuregroups
da_wilcoxonWilcoxon rank-sum test per featuregroups
dirmult_ttestDirichlet-multinomial t-test (ALDEx2-style)groups
lindaLinear models for differential abundance (LinDA)formula

Groups and models. Group methods compare the samples of one categorical variable: groups, a column name of data or one value per sample. Model methods fit a linear model, formula, of any number of variables; groups names its term of interest (the one their plots and post-hoc tests use by default), and groups alone is the same as formula = ~ groups. So da_test(counts, m, 'status', meta) compares the samples by status for every method m, and covariates go in formula: da_test(counts, 'da_lm', 'status', meta, ~ status + age). A one-variable formula works for the group methods too; more than one variable is an error for them.

The methods' assumptions differ, and so do their results: see each method's page. In benchmarks on real data (Nearing et al. 2022; Wirbel et al. 2024; Pelto et al. 2025), the plain per-feature tests (da_wilcoxon(), da_ttest(), da_lm()) controlled false discoveries well, and the methods often disagree: a feature found by several methods is a firmer finding than one found by one.

Flexible name matching

Case insensitive and partial matching, ignoring anything but letters (digits count only to tell 'ANCOM-BC2' from 'ANCOM-BC'). E.g. method = 'Wilcoxon', 'Mann-Whitney' or 'rank sum' selects da_wilcoxon; 't-test' or 'Welch' selects da_ttest; 'lm' or 'linear model' selects da_lm; and 'ALDEx2' selects dirmult_ttest, an ALDEx2-style method (not ALDEx2 itself, whose results agree with it in direction and rough size only).

Finished code should always use the full primary option name to avoid ambiguity with future additions to the list of methods.

Same names in other packages

None known.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Nearing, J. T., Douglas, G. M., Hayes, M. G., et al. (2022). Microbiome differential abundance methods produce different results across 38 datasets. Nature Communications, 13, 342. doi:10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z

Wirbel, J., Essex, M., Forslund, S. K., & Zeller, G. (2024). A realistic benchmark for differential abundance testing and confounder adjustment in human microbiome studies. Genome Biology, 25, 247. doi:10.1186/s13059-024-03390-9

Pelto, J., Auranen, K., Kujala, J. V., & Lahti, L. (2025). Elementary methods provide more replicable results in microbial differential abundance analysis. Briefings in Bioinformatics, 26, bbaf130. doi:10.1093/bib/bbaf130

See also

ancom(), ancombc(), da_lm(), da_ttest(), da_wilcoxon(), dirmult_ttest(), linda(), list_da_tests(); replace_zeros() for the zeros; da_sensitivity() to rerun a method over pseudocounts, zero replacements and scale uncertainties.

Examples

    grp <- c('oral', 'oral', 'other', 'other')
    da_test(ex_counts, 'da_wilcoxon', grp, pseudocount = 1)
#> # A data.frame: 6 × 8
#> # Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test
#>   feature               w   auc median_diff   mean p_value p_adjusted reject
#>   <chr>             <dbl> <dbl>       <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>  <lgl>
#> 1 Streptococcus         4  1           4.43  1.48    0.333          1  FALSE
#> 2 Bacteroides           2  0.5        -1.95  0.141   1              1  FALSE
#> 3 Corynebacterium       0  0          -2.99 -0.689   0.333          1  FALSE
#> 4 Haemophilus           4  1           4.4   0.452   0.333          1  FALSE
#> 5 Propionibacterium     1  0.25       -1.61 -0.686   0.667          1  FALSE
#> 6 Staphylococcus        0  0          -2.28 -0.702   0.333          1  FALSE
#> # Attributes: method, contrast, n, norm, pseudocount, alpha, p_adjust,
#> #   log_base

    # The same comparison by every method, with a model method's covariate.
    meta <- data.frame(site = grp, depth = rowSums(ex_counts))
    da_test(ex_counts + 1, 'da_lm', 'site', meta, ~ site + depth)
#> # A data.frame: 18 × 10
#> # Linear Model
#>    feature           covariate   estimate       se       t  ci_lower ci_upper
#>    <chr>             <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1 Streptococcus     (Intercept)  2.66    0.582      4.58   -4.73     10.1
#>  2 Streptococcus     siteother   -4.76    0.427    -11.2   -10.2       0.659
#>  3 Streptococcus     depth        0.00168 0.000831   2.03   -0.00887   0.0122
#>  4 Bacteroides       (Intercept)  3.14    6.47       0.485 -79        85.3
#>  5 Bacteroides       siteother    3.22    4.74       0.679 -57        63.4
#>  6 Bacteroides       depth       -0.00645 0.00923   -0.699  -0.124     0.111
#>  7 Corynebacterium   (Intercept) -3.72    2.99      -1.24  -41.7      34.3
#>  8 Corynebacterium   siteother    2.5     2.19       1.14  -25.3      30.4
#>  9 Corynebacterium   depth        0.00249 0.00427    0.583  -0.0517    0.0567
#> 10 Haemophilus       (Intercept)  4.43    0.877      5.05   -6.72     15.6
#> 11 Haemophilus       siteother   -3.83    0.643     -5.96  -12         4.34
#> 12 Haemophilus       depth       -0.00289 0.00125   -2.31   -0.0188    0.013
#> 13 Propionibacterium (Intercept) -3.03    3         -1.01  -41.1      35.1
#> 14 Propionibacterium siteother    1.12    2.2        0.51  -26.8      29
#> 15 Propionibacterium depth        0.0025  0.00428    0.583  -0.0519    0.0569
#> 16 Staphylococcus    (Intercept) -3.48    1.94      -1.8   -28.1      21.1
#> 17 Staphylococcus    siteother    1.75    1.42       1.23  -16.3      19.8
#> 18 Staphylococcus    depth        0.00267 0.00276    0.965  -0.0324    0.0377
#> # … 3 more columns: p_value <dbl>, p_adjusted <dbl>, reject <lgl>
#> # Attributes: method, formula, groups, norm, pseudocount, conf_level, alpha,
#> #   p_adjust, log_base, design, dof, mean, resid_sd

    # Which features each method finds.
    x <- rbind(
      c(12, 11, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10), c( 9, 11, 12, 10, 10, 10, 10),
      c( 1, 11, 10, 11, 10,  5,  9), c(22, 21,  9, 10, 10, 10, 10),
      c(20, 22, 10, 10, 13, 10, 10), c(23, 21, 14, 10, 10, 10, 10) )
    colnames(x) <- paste0('b', 1:7)
    meta <- data.frame(trt = rep(c('treatment', 'placebo'), each = 3))
    ids  <- c('ancom', 'da_ttest', 'da_wilcoxon', 'da_lm')
    sapply(ids, function (m) {
      res <- da_test(x, m, 'trt', meta)
      if ('covariate' %in% names(res)) res <- res[res$covariate != '(Intercept)', ]
      res$reject })
#>      ancom da_ttest da_wilcoxon da_lm
